verses.text: The child Samuel ministered to Yahweh before Eli. Yahweh’s word was precious in those days. There visions were not frequent.
At that time, when Eli was laid down in his place (now his eyes had begun to grow dim, so that he could not see),
and God’s lamp hadn’t yet gone out, and Samuel had laid down in Yahweh’s temple, where God’s ark was;
Yahweh called Samuel; and he said, “Here I am.”
He ran to Eli, and said, “Here I am; for you called me.” He said, “I didn’t call. Lie down again.” He went and lay down.
Yahweh called yet again, “Samuel!” Samuel arose and went to Eli, and said, “Here I am; for you called me.” He answered, “I didn’t call, my son. Lie down again.”
Now Samuel didn’t yet know Yahweh, neither was Yahweh’s word yet revealed to him.
Yahweh called Samuel again the third time. He arose and went to Eli, and said, “Here I am; for you called me.” Eli perceived that Yahweh had called the child.
Therefore Eli said to Samuel, “Go, lie down. It shall be, if he calls you, that you shall say, ‘Speak, Yahweh; for your servant hears.’” So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
Yahweh came, and stood, and called as at other times, “Samuel! Samuel!” Then Samuel said, “Speak; for your servant hears.”
Yahweh said to Samuel, “Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of everyone who hears it will tingle.
In that day I will perform against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from the beginning even to the end.
For I have told him that I will judge his house forever, for the iniquity which he knew, because his sons brought a curse on themselves, and he didn’t restrain them.
Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be removed with sacrifice or offering forever.”
Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of Yahweh’s house. Samuel feared to show Eli the vision.
Then Eli called Samuel, and said, “Samuel, my son!” He said, “Here I am.”
He said, “What is the thing that he has spoken to you? Please don’t hide it from me. God do so to you, and more also, if you hide anything from me of all the things that he spoke to you.”
Samuel told him every bit, and hid nothing from him. He said, “It is Yahweh. Let him do what seems good to him.”
Samuel grew, and Yahweh was with him, and let none of his words fall to the ground.
All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of Yahweh.
Yahweh appeared again in Shiloh; for Yahweh revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by Yahweh’s word.

footnotes.content: What a tender picture—young Samuel already serving God before he even knows His voice. The Lord often whispers to those who are simply faithful in small things, staying close.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eli's dimming eyes speak to more than age; they mirror a spiritual dimness too. Yet God never stops reaching out—He sees the young and calls them forth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The lamp of God still burning in the temple—a sacred flame tended through the night. Where prayer and faithfulness are kept, the light never goes out entirely.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God calls, and Samuel answers instantly: "Here I am." That readiness—that open, obedient spirit—is what the Lord loves to see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Samuel runs to Eli—earnest, eager, trying to understand. He doesn't know it's God yet, but his willingness to respond teaches us something about listening closely.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A second call, a second misunderstanding. The Lord is patient with us—He calls again and again until we finally recognize His voice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Samuel didn't yet know Yahweh." The child serves faithfully, yet has never heard God speak directly. Many of us find ourselves there—doing good while still learning what His voice truly sounds like.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The third time brings clarity—not in the child but in the elder. Sometimes we need a wise friend to help us recognize God's hand. Eli finally sees what's happening.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Speak, Yahweh; for your servant hears." Eli teaches Samuel the very words that unlock his calling—a model for how mentors pass faith forward, hand to hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When the Lord calls Samuel by name twice—"Samuel! Samuel!"—it mirrors Abraham, Moses, and others whose callings deepened through that intimacy. God knew him, and now Samuel knows God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God's first words to His new prophet are of judgment—a thing that will make ears tingle. A hard beginning, but the Lord never lies. He trusts Samuel with the truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All that the Lord has spoken about Eli's house will be fulfilled. From beginning to end—nothing is hidden from His sight, nothing escapes His justice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eli knew of his sons' sins but didn't restrain them. Sometimes the saddest judgment falls not on those who stumble, but on those who had the power to speak and stayed silent.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The iniquity shall not be removed with sacrifice." This speaks to a principle deeper than ritual—some stains require more than offering. Only repentance and mercy can wash them clean.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Samuel waits until morning to open the doors—faithful in duty even as fear grips his heart. He hasn't yet learned that the Lord's word, though heavy, carries its own strength.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Samuel, my son!" Eli's tenderness toward this boy—calling him son—shows a love that still reaches out, even though judgment is at his own door.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eli presses Samuel to speak, saying, "Please don't hide it from me." It's a beautiful reminder that we should want truth, even when it costs us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Samuel tells everything without hiding. Eli hears the judgment and responds with surrender: "Let him do what seems good to him." There's a quiet dignity in accepting God's righteous hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Yahweh was with him, and let none of his words fall to the ground." When God establishes a prophet, His word through that vessel doesn't fall empty—it accomplishes what He sends it to do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From Dan to Beersheba—the whole breadth of Israel—Samuel's calling becomes known. God's choice of a prophet is never private; it bears fruit across a people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this closing: God still reveals Himself to those who dwell in His house, still establishes His word through faithful servants. The lamp that burned for young Samuel still burns for us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
